proof_method_executed.structural_audit: 16 gates, 16 passed, 0 failed, entirely within the audited tree. Gated evidence: the RDL declares DATA_IN write-only, the generated subreg instances carry SwAccessWO, the four read arms return register contents anyway, and the same file's other SwAccessWO window (TRIGGER) returns constant zero while no TRIGGER arm returns contents.
proof_method_executed.directed_sim: Unit-level VCS simulation of aes_reg_top over TL-UL. 11 self-checks, 11 passed, 0 errors. Cover counters: all 4 DATA_IN words observed leaking, 1 legitimate control read observed. The recovered 128-bit block matched the written block exactly.
proof_method_executed.negative_control: The identical testbench run against a scratch copy of aes_reg_top.sv with the same file's own treatment of TRIGGER, its other SwAccessWO register, whose read arm at aes_reg_top.sv:1826-1831 returns a constant zero applied to the four DATA_IN arms reports 6 self-check failures, reads 0x00000000 for every word, and drops its leak cover counter to 0, while the control read still succeeds at 1. The testbench therefore discriminates correct RTL from defective RTL, and the failure is attributable to the RTL fix rather than to a broken harness.

result_summary: The write-only AES DATA_IN register window has a software read path. aes_reg_top.sv:1784/1786/1788/1790 return 'reg_rdata_next[31:0] = reg2hw.data_in[i].q' for addr_hit[21..24]. The audited tree contradicts its own specification three times over. First, aes.rdl:68 declares the DATA_IN field 'sw = w' (write-only). Second, the generated instance u_data_in_0 in the same file carries SwAccess(caliptra_prim_subreg_pkg::SwAccessWO), and aes_reg_top.sv is generated from that RDL as its own 'Register Top module auto-generated by reggen' header states. Third and most directly, the file contains 8 SwAccessWO field instances: the 4 DATA_IN words and the 4 TRIGGER bits, and TRIGGER's read arm at lines 1826-1831 returns a constant zero with no arm returning register contents. The same file therefore already demonstrates the correct handling of a write-only window and withholds it only from DATA_IN. The read is genuinely decoded: addr_hit[21] is assigned from AES_DATA_IN_0_OFFSET (0x54) and the four addresses appear in the generated firmware header at 0x10011054 through 0x10011060. In simulation all four words returned the written plaintext, the concatenation reproduced the original 128-bit block, and a repeated read returned the same value, so the exposure is not single-shot.

impact: Software can read back an AES input plaintext block that a more trusted context wrote into the write-only DATA_IN window, recovering all 128 bits with four ordinary MMIO reads.
The exposure is repeatable: nothing in the read path clears the register, so the attacker does not need to win a race against the consuming operation.

The residue persists after the block is consumed. aes_control_fsm.sv:1013 clears only the data_in_new_q tracking flag when the block is loaded into the state register; the register contents are overwritten with pseudo-random data only when software writes the KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR trigger (aes_control_fsm.sv:836, state CTRL_CLEAR_I).

The integration specification treats AES register residue as sensitive and places the clearing duty on firmware: CaliptraIntegrationSpecification.md requires that 'Firmware shall execute the clear operation after any AES operation used to generate or load the MEK' and that firmware clear any obfuscated MEK from memory immediately after use. A read path that exposes the input window undercuts the hardware side of that arrangement during the interval before the clear runs.
security_impact_assessment.bypassed_feature: DATA_IN write-only access: the register block must not return the stored AES input block to software
attacker_model: Privileged software on the Caliptra RISC-V core with MMIO read access to the AES aperture, acting after a more trusted context has staged a plaintext block and before that context executes the clear trigger.

evidence.key_observation: The testbench wrote the recognisable block 0x4f50454e_53454352_45545f50_4c41494e to DATA_IN[0..3] and read back exactly those words from offsets 0x54/0x58/0x5c/0x60, reconstructing 0x4f50454e5345435245545f504c41494e, which is the ASCII text 'OPENSECRET_PLAIN'. None of the reads returned the TL-UL DataWhenError pattern 0xffffffff, so the values are genuine register contents rather than an error response. A second read of DATA_IN[0] returned the same word, confirming reads are non-destructive. Read-arm census inside the file: of its 8 SwAccessWO field instances, the 4 DATA_IN arms return reg2hw.data_in[i].q while all 4 TRIGGER arms return constant zero. On the patched copy every word read 0x00000000 and the recovered block was all zeros.

non_findings.claim: An external SoC agent can read the AES DATA_IN window over AXI.
non_findings.reason: caliptra_top.sv:1135-1147 attaches the AES block to the internal AHB-lite responder fabric via CALIPTRA_SLAVE_SEL_AES (config_defines.svh:60), so the aperture is reachable by software on the Caliptra RISC-V core rather than by external SoC masters. The adversary model is scoped to Caliptra firmware accordingly, which is why the CVSS vector uses PR:H.

non_findings.claim: The leak exposes the AES key.
non_findings.reason: The asset exposed by this read path is the input plaintext block in DATA_IN. The key registers are a separate window; any claim about key share readback belongs to a different finding and is not asserted here.

aes_core.sv:820-821 drives hw2reg.data_in[i].d with prd_clearing_data and its .de with data_in_we, which aes_control_fsm.sv asserts only in state CTRL_CLEAR_I when key_iv_data_in_clear_i is set. The residue therefore lasts until firmware writes the KEY_IV_DATA_IN_CLEAR trigger, not forever. The impact claim is bounded to that interval, which the integration specification acknowledges by requiring firmware to run the clear operation explicitly.

non_findings.claim: The DUT's own SVA confirm the violation.
non_findings.reason: caliptra_prim_onehot_check.AssertConnected_A fires at time 1ps in this harness. It is an init-time check that the integrator bound CALIPTRA_ASSERT_PRIM_COUNT_ERROR_TRIGGER_ALERT, which belongs to block/top-level alert wiring that a unit-level register harness does not instantiate, so it reports on harness structure rather than DUT behaviour. It is compiled in regardless of CLP_ASSERT_ON because caliptra_prim_assert.sv:114 defines CALIPTRA_INC_ASSERT unconditionally under VCS. The proof rests on the testbench's own self-checks, which are independent of the DUT's assertions.

conclusion: Confirmed security bug. A register window that both the RDL and the generated subreg instance declare write-only returns its stored contents on a software read, so an AES input plaintext block staged by a more trusted context is recoverable in full by four MMIO reads, repeatably, until firmware explicitly clears it. The finding rests entirely on evidence inside the audited tree: its own reggen-generated specification, its own SwAccessWO qualifiers, and its own correct handling of an equivalent write-only register in the same file. Proven by 16 structural gates, a directed unit-level simulation that reconstructs the exact 128-bit block with nonzero cover on every word, and a negative control that fails on corrected RTL while its control read still passes.
